data.name: Tarsan
data.gender_notes: Tarsan is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Tarsus was the name of a city founded by Hephaestus. The name Tarsan may have derived from this, with the addition of the suffix ‘-an’, which in Greek means ‘son of’. In Christian tradition, the name Tarsan is linked to the Apostle Tarasius, who was born in the city of Tarsus. He was a prominent bishop in Constantinople and is known for his championing of orthodoxy in the face of various heresies.
data.spiritual_meaning: A strong and steadfast name, reflecting one who stands firm in their faith.
data.etymology: Tarsan belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Tar: a tax or tribute.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tarsan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: טרסן
in_hebrew.meaning: טרסן בן פאולוס, תלמידו של השליח פאולוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם טרסן מופיע בברית החדשה כבן של השליח פאולוס, על פי המסורת הנוצרית, טרסן היה תלמידו של פאולוס ושימש כמלווהו במהלך שליחותו. השם טרסן נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'Ταρσος' (טארסוס), שפירושה 'רגל' או 'כף הרגל', וייתכן כי השם קשור למיקומו הגיאוגרפי של טארסוס, עירו של פאולוס.

in_greek.name: Ταρσαν
in_greek.meaning: Ταρσαν, υιός Παύλου, μαθητής του αποστόλου Παύλου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ταρσαν εμφανίζεται στη Καινή Διαθήκη ως γιος του αποστόλου Παύλου. Σύμφωνα με την χριστιανική παράδοση, ο Ταρσαν ήταν μαθητής του Παύλου και συνόδευε τον απόστολο κατά τη διάρκεια των ιατρικών του περιοδειών. Το όνομα Ταρσαν προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'Ταρσος' (Tarsos), που σημαίνει 'πόδι' ή 'πατούσα', πιθανόν λόγω της γεωγραφικής θέσης της Ταρσού, της πόλης του Παύλου.

in_latin.name: Tarsan
in_latin.meaning: Tarsan, filius Pauli, discipulus apostoli Pauli
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Tarsan in Novo Testamento apparet ut filius apostoli Pauli. Iuxta traditionem christianam, Tarsan fuit discipulus Pauli et comitatus est apostolum durante itinere suo. Nomen Tarsan derivatur ex graeco 'Ταρσος' (Tarsos), quod significat 'pes' vel 'planta pedis', fortasse ob locum geographicum Tarsi, urbem Pauli.

in_english.name: Tarsan
in_english.meaning: Tarsan, a devoted Christian name with apostolic roots
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tarsan originates from the Greek 'Ταρσος' (Tarsos), meaning 'foot' or 'sole'. In Christian tradition, Tarsan is known as the son of Apostle Paul, a devoted disciple who accompanied his father during his missionary journeys. The name Tarsan symbolizes spiritual grounding and apostolic heritage, reflecting a strong connection to early Christian history and the teachings of Saint Paul.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tarsan carries the historical legacy of Greek mythology and the early Christian Church, reflecting a rich cultural heritage. It evokes images of ancient cities, mythical gods, and the spread of the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tarsan connects an individual to the Apostle Tarasius, a man of faith and courage. It symbolizes an unwavering commitment to biblical teachings and a strong stand against heresies and the challenges of faith. The name serves as a reminder of the importance of upholding and defending orthodoxy in one's personal beliefs and in the broader Christian community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tarsan is a name derived from the biblical figure Tarsus, the city where Paul (Apostle) was born. It symbolizes a strong foundation in faith, as Paul was a significant figure in the spread of Christianity. Spiritually, Tarsan represents a deep-rooted commitment to spreading God's word and love.

biblical_reference.note: Tarsus is mentioned as the city of Apostle Paul's origin.

historical_references.reference: According to early Christian tradition, the apostle Tarsan, also known as Tarsus of Cilicia, was one of the twelve apostles. He is said to have been born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, present-day Turkey. Tarsan is believed to have been converted to Christianity by Saint Paul around AD 37-38.

In the Acts of the Apostles, an account of the early Christian church written by Luke c. AD 60-63, it is mentioned that Paul and Barnabas visited Tarsus to recruit Tarsan to join them in their missionary journey. This occurred around AD 46.
